_note: The book prints the six substrates as DRAWN skeletal/valence structures, not as condensed formulae. They are rendered here as condensed formulae so the row is self-contained; each rendering was checked against the book's own printed IUPAC name for that item and all six reconcile, so no figure crop is required. The drawings also fix the alkene geometry (cis/trans), which the printed answers do not use — no E/Z descriptor appears in the book's solution.

stem: Identify all the possible monochloro structural isomers expected to be formed on free radical monochlorination of \((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3\).
solution:
In the given molecule, there are four different types of hydrogen atoms. Replacement of these hydrogen atoms will give the following:

\((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}\)

\((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}(\text{Cl})\text{CH}_3\)

\((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}(\text{Cl})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3\)

\(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_2\text{Cl})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3\)

stem:
Write the products of the following reactions:

(i) \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \rightarrow\)

(ii) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HCl} \rightarrow\)

(iii) \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \xrightarrow{\text{Peroxide}}\)
_note: The book draws the phenyl group of (i) and (iii) as a benzene ring and prints the products as drawn structures; rendered here as condensed formulae. Item (iii) carries "Peroxide" over the arrow, which is what makes it the anti-Markovnikov (peroxide-effect) product while (i) and (ii) follow Markovnikov's rule.

stem: Haloalkanes react with KCN to form alkyl cyanides as main product while AgCN forms isocyanides as the chief product. Explain.
solution: KCN is predominantly ionic and provides cyanide ions in solution. Although both carbon and nitrogen atoms are in a position to donate electron pairs, the attack takes place mainly through carbon atom and not through nitrogen atom since C—C bond is more stable than C—N bond. However, AgCN is mainly covalent in nature and nitrogen is free to donate electron pair forming isocyanide as the main product.
